title: Are You Experienced
note: Hendrix's debut album fused blues, psychedelia and feedback, setting a new standard for electric guitar.

title: Axis: Bold as Love
note: A second album in 1967 that deepened Hendrix's studio experiments and ballad writing.

title: Electric Ladyland
note: Sprawling double album and Hendrix's last studio record released in his lifetime.

title: Led Zeppelin
note: Debut that fused blues with heavy volume and became a template for hard rock.
dateNote: US release date; UK release followed on 1969-03-31

title: The Stooges
note: Raw proto-punk debut produced by John Cale.

title: Led Zeppelin II
note: Heavy riffs, including 'Whole Lotta Love', that pushed hard rock toward heavy metal.

title: Black Sabbath
note: Often cited as the first heavy metal album, built on doom, tritones and a horror-film atmosphere.

title: Fun House
note: The Stooges' second album, more ferocious and raw than their debut.

title: Paranoid
note: Sabbath's breakthrough, containing the title track, 'Iron Man' and 'War Pigs' and cementing the template of metal.

title: Led Zeppelin III
note: Zeppelin's acoustic-leaning folk-rock turn alongside heavier moments.

title: Master of Reality
note: Sabbath tuned down further, creating a sludgier sound later called doom and stoner.

title: Who's Next
note: Synthesisers and power chords fused in the Who's biggest-selling studio album.

title: Led Zeppelin IV
note: Includes 'Black Dog' and 'Stairway to Heaven', and is among the best-selling albums of all time.

title: The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars
note: Bowie's glam rock concept album introduced the Ziggy persona and its theatrical rock stagecraft.

title: Vol. 4
note: Sabbath's fourth album ('Snowblind', 'Supernaut') was recorded in Los Angeles and was heavier and more experimental.

title: Raw Power
note: Iggy and the Stooges' third album, mixed by Bowie; a direct precursor of punk.

title: Houses of the Holy
note: Zeppelin expanded their sound with funk, reggae and progressive touches.

title: Aladdin Sane
note: Bowie's follow-up to Ziggy, with a more aggressive piano and guitar attack.

title: Pin Ups
note: Bowie's album of covers of 1960s British rock songs.

title: Quadrophenia
note: The Who's second rock opera, about a mod youth in 1960s Britain.

title: Sabbath Bloody Sabbath
note: Sabbath's fifth album mixed progressive and heavy styles, with Rick Wakeman guesting.

title: Diamond Dogs
note: Bowie's dystopian glam album, partly inspired by Orwell's 1984.

title: High Voltage (Australian version)
note: AC/DC's Australian-only debut, recorded quickly in early 1975.

title: Physical Graffiti
note: Zeppelin's sprawling double album, including 'Kashmir'.

title: Young Americans
note: Bowie's 'plastic soul' album, including the hit 'Fame'.

title: Sabotage
note: Sabbath's heaviest effort of the mid-70s, recorded during a legal battle with their former management.

title: The Who by Numbers
note: A downbeat, introspective Who album written largely by Pete Townshend.

title: T.N.T.
note: AC/DC's second album, Australian release, with anthems 'High Voltage' and 'T.N.T.'.

title: Station to Station
note: Bowie's transitional album between soul and the electronic, krautrock-influenced Berlin period.

title: Sad Wings of Destiny
note: Priest's second album introduced the dual-guitar attack and operatic vocals that became a metal template.

title: Presence
note: A guitar-driven Zeppelin album recorded while Robert Plant recovered from a car accident.

title: High Voltage (international version)
note: The international compilation of AC/DC's first two Australian albums.

title: Ramones
note: Fourteen songs in under thirty minutes; the Ramones' debut kicked off American punk and its stripped-down speed.

title: Dirty Deeds Done Dirt Cheap
note: AC/DC's third album, with Bon Scott's lecherous humour front and centre.

title: Leave Home
note: The Ramones' second album repeated the formula, with 'Pinhead' and 'Carbona Not Glue'.

title: Low
note: First of Bowie's Berlin trilogy, co-produced with Brian Eno.

title: Let There Be Rock
note: AC/DC's fourth album, with a high-energy, blues-based hard rock sound.

title: Sin After Sin
note: Priest's Columbia debut, produced by Roger Glover, with drummer Simon Phillips.

title: Motörhead
note: Motörhead's self-titled debut, a loud, fast mix of punk and metal.

title: "Heroes"
note: Bowie's second Berlin album, with Robert Fripp's guitar and the title track.

title: Never Mind the Bollocks, Here's the Sex Pistols
note: The Pistols' only studio album; a defining punk record and a public scandal.

title: Rocket to Russia
note: The Ramones' third album, including 'Sheena Is a Punk Rocker' and 'Rockaway Beach'.

title: Stained Class
note: Priest's heavy, concise 1978 album, later at the centre of a 1990 court case.

title: Van Halen
note: Eddie Van Halen's guitar on this debut, particularly 'Eruption', changed rock guitar playing.

title: Powerage
note: A tougher, bluesier AC/DC record, highly regarded by fans and by Keith Richards.

title: Who Are You
note: The final Who album featuring drummer Keith Moon, who died weeks after its release.

title: Road to Ruin
note: The Ramones' fourth album, with 'I Wanna Be Sedated'.

title: Killing Machine (US: Hell Bent for Leather)
listTitle: Killing Machine / Hell Bent for Leather
note: Priest streamlined their sound and adopted their leather-and-studs look.

title: Van Halen II
note: Van Halen's second album, including 'Dance the Night Away'.

title: Overkill
note: Motörhead's second album; its double-bass-drum title track is often cited as an ancestor of speed and thrash metal.

title: Lodger
note: The third and last of Bowie's Berlin albums.

title: Saxon
note: Saxon's self-titled debut introduced their blue-collar metal.

title: Highway to Hell
note: Last album with Bon Scott, and AC/DC's international breakthrough.

title: In Through the Out Door
note: Zeppelin's last studio album before Bonham's death.

title: Bomber
note: Motörhead's third album, including the title track and a stage lighting rig in the shape of a bomber.

title: The Soundhouse Tapes
note: Maiden's self-released first EP, helped by Neal Kay's Soundhouse sound system.

title: On Parole
note: Motörhead's first album recorded in 1975, shelved by the label and released in 1979.

title: Beware
note: An early Misfits EP released on the band's own label.

title: End of the Century
note: Ramones album produced by Phil Spector, with 'Baby, I Love You'.

title: Women and Children First
note: Van Halen's third album, a heavier follow-up.

title: Wheels of Steel
note: Saxon's second album, and an NWOBHM landmark with the title anthem.

title: British Steel
note: Priest's stripped-down commercial breakthrough, with 'Breaking the Law' and 'Living After Midnight'.

title: Iron Maiden
note: Maiden's debut, with Paul Di'Anno, brought punk-edge to the NWOBHM.

title: Heaven and Hell
note: Sabbath's first album with Ronnie James Dio proved the band could survive Ozzy's exit.

title: Back in Black
note: AC/DC's tribute to Bon Scott and Brian Johnson's debut; one of the best-selling albums ever.

title: Scary Monsters (and Super Creeps)
note: Bowie's last classic album of his 70s run, with 'Ashes to Ashes'.

title: Blizzard of Ozz
note: Ozzy's solo debut, with Randy Rhoads' guitar and 'Crazy Train' and 'Mr. Crowley'.

title: Ace of Spades
note: Motörhead's best-known album, whose title track is a speed-metal anthem.

title: Strong Arm of the Law
note: Saxon's third album and their consolidation of the NWOBHM sound.

title: Killers
note: Maiden's second album, the last with Paul Di'Anno.

title: Point of Entry
note: Priest's more commercial 1981 album.

title: Fair Warning
note: Van Halen's darkest and heaviest album.

title: Pleasant Dreams
note: A Ramones album that drifted toward pop.

title: Denim and Leather
note: Saxon's fourth album, with the fan-anthem title track.

title: Mob Rules
note: Sabbath's second Dio-fronted album; its title track also appeared in the 1981 animated film Heavy Metal.

title: Diary of a Madman
note: Ozzy's second solo album and Randy Rhoads' last.

title: Too Fast for Love
note: Mötley Crüe's self-released debut, the start of their glam-metal ascent.

title: For Those About to Rock
note: AC/DC's follow-up to Back in Black, with its cannon-fire title track.

title: Welcome to Hell
note: Venom's raw, Satanic debut was a blueprint for extreme metal.

title: Troops of Tomorrow
note: The Exploited's second album, a mix of punk and metal.

title: Walk Among Us
note: The Misfits' first full-length album, a fixture of horror-punk.

title: The Number of the Beast
note: Maiden's first with Bruce Dickinson; its title track and 'Hallowed Be Thy Name' became classics.

title: Power Metal
note: A Metallica demo with early songs from 1982.

title: Diver Down
note: Van Halen's cover-heavy album.

title: Iron Fist
note: The last Motörhead album with 'Fast' Eddie Clarke.

title: No Life 'til Leather
note: Metallica's 1982 demo, copied by tape traders around the world.

title: Screaming for Vengeance
note: Priest's American breakthrough, with 'You've Got Another Thing Comin''.

title: Black Metal
note: Venom's second album gave an entire genre its name.

title: Subterranean Jungle
note: Ramones' eighth studio album.

title: Power & the Glory
note: Saxon's classic NWOBHM album.

title: Let's Dance
note: Bowie's commercial peak, produced by Nile Rodgers.

title: Piece of Mind
note: Maiden's first album with Nicko McBrain.

title: Another Perfect Day
note: Motörhead's only album with Brian Robertson on guitar.

title: Kill 'Em All
note: Metallica's debut, with its fast, aggressive riffs, kicked off American thrash metal.

title: Flick of the Switch
note: AC/DC's stripped-down 1983 album.

title: Shout at the Devil
note: Mötley Crüe's second album mixed glam and metal imagery.

title: Bark at the Moon
note: Ozzy's first with Jake E. Lee.

title: Earth A.D./Wolfs Blood
note: The Misfits' faster, metal-leaning last Danzig-era album.

title: Show No Mercy
note: Slayer's debut, on Metal Blade, set out their fast, Satanic style.
Van Halen's biggest-selling album, with 'Jump'.

title: Fistful of Metal
note: Anthrax's debut, with Neil Turbin on vocals.

title: At War with Satan
note: Venom's progressive, side-long title track experiment.

title: Haunting the Chapel
note: Slayer's EP that shows a heavier sound ahead of Hell Awaits.

title: Ride the Lightning
note: Metallica's second album brought more complex songs, acoustic passages and melody to thrash.

title: Powerslave
note: Maiden's Egyptian-themed album, with 'Aces High' and 'Rime of the Ancient Mariner'.

title: Reign of Terror
note: Death's 1984 demo, made as Chuck Schuldiner's band changed its name from Mantas.

title: Too Tough to Die
note: Ramones' return to a harder, punkier sound.

title: Possessed
note: Venom's fourth album, with the title track later targeted by the PMRC.

title: Hell Awaits
note: Slayer's second album, darker and more complex.

title: Bonded by Blood
note: Exodus's debut is a landmark of Bay Area thrash.

title: Killing Is My Business... and Business Is Good!
note: Megadeth's debut, recorded on a tiny budget, with intricate, aggressive riffing.
dateNote: The owner's date is the 1985-06-12 US release; the UK release by Music for Nations was 1985-05-17

title: Theatre of Pain
note: Mötley Crüe's glam-leaning third album, with 'Home Sweet Home'.

title: Fly on the Wall
note: A harder and less successful AC/DC album.

title: Crab Society North
note: S.O.D.'s early demo that preceded their debut album.

title: Speak English or Die
note: S.O.D.'s debut mixed thrash, hardcore and crude humour, helping to create crossover.

title: Seven Churches
note: Possessed's debut is widely cited as a foundational death metal album.

title: Spreading the Disease
note: Anthrax's first with singer Joey Belladonna.

title: The Ultimate Sin
note: Ozzy's mid-80s album, with the glossy production of Ron Nevison.

title: Master of Puppets
note: Metallica's third album, the pinnacle of thrash and their last with Cliff Burton.

title: Peace Sells... but Who's Buying?
note: Megadeth's second album, with Mustaine's acid riffing and the title-track bassline.

title: Somewhere in Time
note: Maiden's synthesiser-infused album.

title: Reign in Blood
note: Slayer's 29-minute classic, produced by Rick Rubin, defined speed and brutality in metal.

title: Beyond the Gates
note: Possessed's second album, with a more technical approach.

title: Morbid Visions
note: Sepultura's debut, raw death and thrash metal from Brazil.

title: Among the Living
note: Anthrax's breakthrough, with 'Caught in a Mosh' and 'Indians'.

title: Girls, Girls, Girls
note: Mötley Crüe's fourth album.

title: Scream Bloody Gore
note: Death's debut is widely called the first true death metal album.
dateNote: Official title is 'Scream Bloody Gore'; the list has 'Screaming Bloody Gore'

title: Pleasures of the Flesh
note: Exodus's second album, the first with Steve Souza.

title: Schizophrenia
note: Sepultura's second album, where the band's sound began to develop.

title: Blow Up Your Video
note: AC/DC's late-80s return to form.

title: Seventh Son of a Seventh Son
listTitle: Seventh Son of a Seventh Son
note: Maiden's progressive concept album.

title: South of Heaven
note: Slayer's slower, more atmospheric follow-up to Reign in Blood.

title: Leprosy
note: Death's second album, which cemented the Florida death metal sound.

title: ...And Justice for All
note: Metallica's first album with Jason Newsted, with long, complex songs and a famously dry mix.

title: State of Euphoria
note: Anthrax's 1988 album, including 'Make Me Laugh'.

title: Fabulous Disaster
note: Exodus's third album, with a more polished sound.

title: Beneath the Remains
note: Sepultura's international breakthrough, on Roadrunner.

title: Spiritual Healing
note: Death's third album, with more mature lyrics and a more complex sound.

title: Impact Is Imminent
note: Exodus's fourth album, with a technical thrash style.

title: Persistence of Time
note: Anthrax's darker album.

title: The Razors Edge
note: AC/DC's comeback, with 'Thunderstruck'.

title: Seasons in the Abyss
note: Slayer's heavy, mid-tempo late-era classic.

title: Arise
note: Sepultura's fourth album, a blend of thrash and death.

title: Human
note: Death's fourth album, a step toward progressive and technical death metal.

title: Individual Thought Patterns
note: Death's fifth album, a technical high point.

title: Divine Intervention
note: Slayer's 1994 album, the first without Dave Lombardo.
